title: Feedback Loops — Mathematical Form vs. Neurological Implementation
content_html:
Feedback Loops

Mathematical Form vs. Neurological Implementation

Mathematical Actualisation

x(t+1) = f(x(t)) + K·e(t) + ε where e(t) = u(t) - y(t)

  • Negative feedback (stabilising): gain K reduces error and drives the system toward a setpoint.
  • Positive feedback (amplifying): reinforces deviations; useful for switching and phase transitions.
  • Control theory: PID regulators, state‑space models, Lyapunov stability; noise and delay explicitly modelled.
  • Bayesian update: Posterior ∝ Likelihood × Prior; prediction error drives parameter/state updates.

Formal tools: differential/difference equations, transfer functions, Kalman filters, stochastic control.

Neurological Actualisation

  • Predictive coding loops: top‑down predictions vs. bottom‑up signals; cortical hierarchies minimise prediction error.
  • Excitatory–inhibitory balance: local negative feedback stabilises firing; disinhibition gates positive loops for learning.
  • Cortico–striatal–dopamine loops: reward prediction error (δ) updates policies (reinforcement learning analogue).
  • Cortico–thalamic loops: thalamus modulates gain/attention; recurrent routing shapes perception.
  • Hippocampal–cortical loops: consolidation/reconsolidation update memory traces with new context.

Mechanisms: spike‑timing dependent plasticity (STDP), neuromodulators (DA, NE, ACh), homeostatic scaling.

Alignment Map

  • Error signal ↔ Prediction error (sensory minus predicted input)
  • Controller gain (K) ↔ Neuromodulatory gain (dopamine, norepinephrine adjusting plasticity/precision)
  • Negative feedback ↔ Inhibitory interneurons / homeostatic plasticity (stability)
  • Positive feedback ↔ Hebbian/STDP potentiation (learning & amplification)
  • State estimator (Kalman) ↔ Recurrent cortical inference (belief updating under uncertainty)
  • Setpoint / objective ↔ Goals / priors (task demands, survival needs)
  • Noise & delay models ↔ Neural variability & conduction delay

Worked Intuitions

  • Thermostat ↔ Cortical inhibition: inhibitory circuits keep activity near functional ranges (homeostasis).
  • Kalman filter ↔ Sensorimotor control: cerebellar/cortical circuits integrate predictions with sensory input to reduce movement error.
  • TD learning ↔ Dopamine: phasic dopamine encodes reward prediction error δ, adjusting future action values.
